target_meaning: faces, dark center, no light penetration at the center
produced_reading: Face perimeter/surface is dark at the center (center of faces is dark). Combines F (faces) with dark and ctr (center). Contrast with the negotiated 'dark-center' symptom from Type 14 Core Void, but applied with F prefix rather than as standalone.
All parts/everything shows a wavering quality. A is not a negotiated positional prefix in our code; H-waver is the negotiated hum code. Best reading: all-over wavering (sound or light).
All-over warm temperature sensation. A prefix not negotiated for positional use; warm is not in our negotiated suffix list (HOT/COLD are). Decoded as: overall warmth across all surfaces.
Faces producing a clicking sound. Combines F (faces) with click. Click is a negotiated hum descriptor (H-click) but applied here to face behavior, which is unusual.
Faces appear curved or bulging. Combines F (faces) with CURVED (negotiated standalone for bulging/distortion). Plausible extension of CURVED to specifically describe face distortion.
Corners are warping or distorting. Combines C (corners) with warp (negotiated edge descriptor E-warp). Applied to corners instead of edges.
Face light patterns are wavering/unstable. Combines F (faces) with waver. Waver is negotiated as H-waver (hum descriptor); here applied to face behavior.
Hum sounds dim or faint/reduced in intensity. Combines H (hum) with dim. Dim is negotiated for faces/light; applied here to hum quality as low/faint sound.
Hum is flickering or cutting in and out irregularly. Combines H (hum) with flicker. Flicker is negotiated for faces (F-flicker); applied here to hum behavior.
Face light patterns appear thin or weak/shallow. Combines F (faces) with thin. Thin is negotiated as H-thin (hum descriptor); applied here to face light quality.
Edges are flickering or flashing. Combines E (edges) with flicker. Flicker is a negotiated face descriptor (F-flicker); applied here to edges.
Hum has a clicking or ticking quality. Combines H (hum) with click. Directly negotiated in our code table as a hum descriptor.
Corners sound or feel hollow. Combines C (corners) with hollow. HOLLOW is a negotiated standalone descriptor for the whole Veyru sounding hollow when tapped; applied here specifically to corners.
Hum has a warm quality (tone or temperature-associated sound change). Combines H (hum) with warm. Warm is not a negotiated suffix; HOT/COLD are the negotiated temperature codes.
Face patterns appear blurred or smearing. Combines F (faces) with blur. Blur is negotiated as E-blur (edge descriptor); applied here to face patterns.
Hum has a curved or warped tonal quality (metaphorical). Combines H (hum) with CURVED (negotiated standalone for physical bulging). Cross-domain application.
Hum is warping or bending in tone. Combines H (hum) with warp. Warp is negotiated as E-warp (edge descriptor); applied here to hum behavior.
Hum is associated with heat or the heat is audible in the hum quality. Combines H (hum) with HOT (negotiated standalone temperature descriptor). Cross-domain application.
Edges produce a clicking or ticking sound. Combines E (edges) with click. Click is negotiated as H-click (hum descriptor); applied here to edge behavior.
Edges are splitting or showing a divided/bifurcated appearance. Combines E (edges) with split. Split is negotiated as H-split (hum descriptor); applied here to edges.
Corners are noticeably bright or glowing intensely. Combines C (corners) with bright. Directly negotiated in our code table as a corner descriptor.
Edges sound or feel hollow. Combines E (edges) with hollow. HOLLOW is a negotiated standalone; applied here specifically to edges.
